cards.title: What is media?
cards.text: Media are the channels that carry news and information, such as newspapers, TV, radio and the internet.

cards.title: Role of journalism
cards.text: Journalists gather facts, check them and report so citizens can make informed choices.

cards.title: Misinformation
cards.text: Misinformation is false information spread, often by mistake. Disinformation is spread on purpose.

cards.title: Spotting fake news
cards.text: Check the source, look for other reports, read beyond headlines and be wary of shocking claims.

qs.q: A step to spot fake news is…

cards.title: Why fake news spreads
cards.text: Shocking posts get clicks and shares, so lies can travel faster than corrections.

cards.title: Echo chambers
cards.text: Social feeds show you what you already like, so you may only see one side.

cards.title: Influencers
cards.text: Influencers shape tastes and opinions. Ask whether they are paid to promote things.

qs.q: Before trusting an influencer, check if…

cards.title: Media bias
cards.text: Bias is when reporting favours one side. Reading different outlets gives a fuller picture.

cards.title: Sensationalism
cards.text: Exaggerating to grab attention can mislead people and create fear.

cards.title: Privacy and the press
cards.text: Reporting should not cruelly invade private lives, especially of victims and children.

cards.title: Social media and news
cards.text: Many get news from social media, but posts may be unchecked. Verify before sharing.

qs.q: Before sharing a post, you should…

cards.title: Digital media habits
cards.text: Balanced use means choosing quality content and taking breaks.

cards.title: Heritage
cards.text: Heritage is the buildings, art and traditions inherited from the past that we should protect.

cards.title: Why preserve culture
cards.text: Culture gives identity and connects generations. Once lost, it is hard to recover.

cards.title: Regional languages
cards.text: Languages carry stories and ways of thinking. When languages vanish, culture is lost.

cards.title: Folk arts
cards.text: Folk dances, music and crafts reflect local life and give work to artisans.

cards.title: Museums
cards.text: Museums protect objects and tell stories of the past to new generations.

cards.title: Tourism and heritage
cards.text: Tourism brings income but crowds can damage fragile sites. Responsible tourism protects them.

cards.title: Art as expression
cards.text: Art lets people share feelings and ideas, and sometimes challenge society.

cards.title: Classical arts
cards.text: Classical dance and music need years of training and keep old traditions alive.

cards.title: Cultural exchange
cards.text: Sharing food, films and festivals across cultures increases understanding.

cards.title: Handicrafts
cards.text: Handloom and handicrafts keep rural livelihoods alive. Buying local helps.

cards.title: Language and identity
cards.text: Speaking many languages is an advantage. Mother tongue and English can coexist.

cards.title: Youth and traditions
cards.text: Young people can keep traditions alive by learning them and giving them a modern twist.

qs.q: Youth can keep traditions alive by…

cards.title: Freedom of expression
cards.text: People may share their views freely, but not to spread hate or harm others.

qs.q: Free speech has limits when it…

cards.title: Censorship
cards.text: Censorship is controlling what people can say or see. Too much stifles ideas; some limits protect from harm.

cards.title: Media influence on youth
cards.text: Media shapes what young people wear, want and believe. Critical viewing is needed.

cards.title: Advertising
cards.text: Ads persuade us to buy. Ask whether you need the product or are being nudged.

cards.title: Body image
cards.text: Edited pictures set unrealistic standards and hurt self-esteem. Real people look different.

cards.title: Creativity
cards.text: Creativity means producing new ideas. Technology gives everyone tools to create.

cards.title: Films and society
cards.text: Films reflect and shape society, spreading both good and harmful ideas.

cards.title: Copyright
cards.text: Copyright protects creators’ work. Copying without permission is unfair.

cards.title: Online hate
cards.text: Hate speech online hurts people and divides communities. Report it, don’t spread it.

cards.title: Responsible sharing
cards.text: Think before posting: is it true, kind and necessary?

qs.q: Before posting, ask if it is…

cards.title: Public broadcasting
cards.text: Public media aims to inform and educate, not just entertain.

cards.title: Media literacy
cards.text: Media literacy is the skill of understanding, questioning and using media wisely.
